s1.syndrome_frame: A subacute onset of a painful breast mass with associated imaging and histopathological findings
salient_findings: Palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
Ill-defined, deep retroareolar spiculated lesion on breast MRI
Cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells within a dense lymphoid infiltrate on excisional biopsy
key_facts: One-month history of burning sensation and discomfort in the left breast
No fever or systemic symptoms
Hypertension and history of hemorrhoidectomy, dilation and curettage, colonoscopy, and gastroscopy
Heavy smoker
3 × 3 cm palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
No axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
Unremarkable routine blood tests, chest radiograph, and ECG
Breast MRI showed an ill-defined, deep retroareolar spiculated lesion
Excisional biopsy showed breast tissue with cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells
Epithelial cells positive for cytokeratin AE1/E3 and negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu
Background lymphocytes stained positive for CD3 and CD20

shortlist.label: Medullary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Triple-negative breast cancer with lymphoid infiltrate and spiculated lesion on MRI

shortlist.label: Lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells within a dense lymphoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: Triple-negative breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Epithelial cells negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu

shortlist.label: Carcinoma with lymphoid stroma
shortlist.why_kept: Breast tissue containing cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells within a dense lymphoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: Primary breast lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dense lymphoid infiltrate and positive staining for CD3 and CD20

raw.rationale: The presence of a palpable mass, ill-defined spiculated lesion on breast MRI, and excisional biopsy showing cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells with a dense lymphoid infiltrate, along with the epithelial cells being negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu, are consistent with medullary carcinoma, a subtype of triple-negative breast cancer known for its lymphoid infiltrate and poor prognosis.

rejected.label: Lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: While it shares some features with the case, lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma is less common and typically has a distinct epidemiological and pathological profile that doesn't perfectly match the provided case details.

rejected.label: Triple-negative breast cancer
rejected.why: Too broad, as medullary carcinoma is a specific subtype of triple-negative breast cancer that better explains the lymphoid infiltrate and specific pathological features described.

rejected.label: Carcinoma with lymphoid stroma
rejected.why: This term is more general and could encompass several entities, including medullary carcinoma, but doesn't specifically capture the distinct clinicopathological features of the case as well as medullary carcinoma does.

rejected.label: Primary breast lymphoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results showing cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells and the absence of diagnostic features specific to lymphoma (such as a predominant lymphoid population with atypia or specific lymphoma markers) make this diagnosis less likely.
